candidates.title: Replace per-order export reads with batched item loading
candidates.problem: Exports issue one item query for every selected order. Source proves repeated database work contrary to the export contract; its latency and production frequency are unknown.
candidates.fix: Load export items in batches and assemble the existing order response.

instances.quote: return [{'id': order.id, 'items': db.query('SELECT * FROM items WHERE order_id = ?', order.id)} for order in orders]

candidates.root_cause: list_orders queries items inside the order comprehension
candidates.verification: Proposed: use 0, 1 and 25 orders with mixed item counts; assert equivalent response contents and batched item-query count instead of one query per order. No check ran here.
candidates.invariant: Order exports must batch item reads rather than query once per exported order.
candidates.scenario: For an export returning N orders, list_orders performs N item reads after the initial order query, with no limit or batch in the enclosing function.

trace.quote: return [{'id': order.id, 'items': db.query('SELECT * FROM items WHERE order_id = ?', order.id)} for order in orders]

candidates.flow: export_orders passes list_orders(db) to response.write; list_orders selects all order ids then consumes each id through a separate item query. The separate preview function has a LIMIT 5 and does not enclose this export path.
remediation: Choose a bounded batch size compatible with database parameter limits.
Fetch items for each batch and preserve each order and its items in the existing response shape.
Verify equivalent results and operation counts on the bounded proposed cases.
candidates.compatibility: Preserve order ids, empty item lists and response ordering; leave the accepted preview behavior intact.
candidates.rollback: Restore the previous list_orders implementation if response compatibility fails; no schema change is needed.

candidates.title: Page catalog reads before materializing all products
candidates.problem: The catalog reads and filters every product to display 20. Supplied synthetic executed evidence attributes 82% of sampled request CPU to materialization and filtering for its single workload; this does not establish production impact.
candidates.fix: Fetch a bounded public-product page at the store boundary.
candidates.root_cause: catalog_page materializes all products before public filtering and slicing
candidates.verification: Proposed: compare current and paged outputs on 0, 19, 20 and 25 public products mixed with private products; assert no private products escape and at most the requested page is returned from the store. A separately authorized replay of the supplied workload should verify bounded materialization; no speedup target or executed result is asserted.
candidates.invariant: The public catalog page should fetch only the visible page rather than materialize the entire catalog.
candidates.scenario: The supplied 100000-product synthetic workload materializes all records and filters public products before the visible first page reaches render.
candidates.flow: catalog_page invokes store.all_products, filters the returned products for public visibility on line 3, then renders the first 20. The supplied profile names these same materialization and filtering steps.
remediation: Define a store page API that filters public products before applying the page limit.
Switch catalog_page to the bounded API while preserving current ordering and rendering inputs.
Verify visibility and output equivalence on bounded fixtures before any separately authorized measurement.
candidates.compatibility: Store implementation is unavailable; confirm ordering and filtering semantics before choosing its pagination API.
candidates.rollback: Keep the old store API during rollout and restore catalog_page to it if compatibility checks fail.
